title: Young-feminine Japanese voice variant bake-off
question: Can a bounded Extension-routed comparison of youthful-feminine Japanese voice variants identify a shortlist that is materially more natural and useful than the rejected MS-2 voices?
hypothesis: Reviewing authorized youthful-feminine voice/style references across several protocol-v1 voice-conversion families before longer training work will yield at least two useful shortlist candidates while preserving exact route identity and native fallback.

control.description: The same source content remains on the native ChatGPT voice route and is rated in the same operator session.

variants.description: Nine to twelve immutable, primarily youthful-feminine Japanese voice variants from at least four families, each eligible only after Gateway-to-Extension route parity.

fixtures.manifest: Freeze an authorized 10-utterance Japanese screen and the existing 40-utterance comparison corpus before approval; prompt text and metadata may be versioned, but raw captured/reference/output audio stays outside Git.

environment.git_commit: Persist counted receipts only from the exact clean checked-out commit.
environment.runtime: One content-addressed deployment bundle loaded by the loopback Gateway, verified by the terminal launcher, and fetched by the unpacked Extension.
environment.hardware: One leased GPU at a time; record only non-sensitive hardware class and runtime revisions.

model_revisions.variants: Freeze profile, configuration, pack/evidence, implementation, weights, training-data lineage, authorization, and bundle digests before a variant becomes listenable.

procedure.summary: Review license and voice authorization before material acquisition. Count only protocol-v1 audio-to-audio voice-conversion variants in the first wave. Build isolated static profiles, generate one immutable deployment bundle, verify the same bundle through terminal, Gateway, and Extension, and require a route-parity receipt before displaying a variant. Exclude one warmup, screen every eligible variant on the same 10 utterances through the actual Extension, retain route failures and quality rejections, freeze a shortlist of at most four and at most two per family, and hand that shortlist to the full 40-utterance MS-4 comparison. Qwen and CosyVoice TTS candidates remain deferred until an accepted ADR defines committed spoken text, transport, interruption, and played-text accounting.
procedure.warmup: Exclude one declared cold initialization per variant. Record cold time separately and do not use warmup output for listening scores.
commands: LV-056 freezes the deployment-bundle build and terminal/Gateway/Extension parity commands before experiment approval
LV-060 freezes the screen runner and metadata-only receipt command before GPU execution
invalidation_conditions: The candidate catalog, fixture, deployment bundle, or listening order changes after experiment approval.
A counted result came from direct worker or terminal output instead of the authenticated Gateway-to-Extension route.
The terminal launcher, Gateway, Extension, or receipt resolves a different bundle, profile, configuration, pack, voice, training-data, or authorization identity.
A target voice, style, checkpoint, training corpus, or preset lacks an explicit license and authorization disposition.

A public authorization digest cannot be resolved to the exact approved, nonexpired record in the operator-controlled private registry, or its variant, family, profile, source, terms, or lineage binding differs.
Raw captured, reference, or generated audio; credentials; host paths; voice IDs; weights; or private operator notes enter Git or a public manifest.
Native and remote audio overlap, stale output is accepted, native fallback is unavailable, or any expected-path queue becomes unbounded.
A TTS result is described as voice conversion, or a terminal-only/debug result is described as Extension-listenable.
A text-to-speech candidate is counted before an accepted committed-spoken-text transport ADR and shared protocol contract exist.
Screening selects a winner, admits more than four variants, admits more than two variants from one family, or hides failed attempts.
A quality, latency, speaker, content, security, or release pass is claimed from an unassessed lane.

decision_rule: This screening experiment never selects a final model. It may freeze an MS-4 shortlist only after 9 to 12 protocol-v1 voice-conversion variants from at least four families are actually heard through the same bundle-bound Extension route on all 10 screen utterances, every attempt and route failure is retained, no hard authorization/content/integrity/route-safety failure is hidden, and the shortlist contains at most four variants and at most two from one family. Prefer variants the named operator marks keep and scores at least 3/5 for intelligibility, naturalness, youthful-feminine fit, and conversational usefulness. TTS does not count unless a later accepted ADR and protocol revision explicitly admit it. If fewer than two variants are worth continuing, approve at most one bounded second wave instead of declaring a winner or beginning open-ended tuning.

artifact_policy.raw_location: Authorized source/reference material, weights, captured audio, and optional output renders stay in the ignored artifact store or ephemeral process memory.
artifact_policy.git_contents: Plan, candidate catalog, schemas, public-safe provenance URLs, immutable digests, aggregate route facts, and operator scores without raw audio or free-form sensitive notes.
artifact_policy.retention: Delete temporary output audio after the listening decision or within 14 days; retain only authorized source artifacts needed to reproduce shortlisted profiles.
artifact_policy.authorization: Every preset, reference, training set, checkpoint, and model receives separate code, weight, data, attribution, notice, and target-voice authorization review before use.
